diagnosis.summary: The attempt never got past OS package installation. All three nodes (Ubuntu 16.04/xenial) spent the entire ~35-minute run repeatedly failing to download rabbitmq-server/erlang packages from archive.ubuntu.com and security.ubuntu.com, and the executor's global timeout (2100s) hit while apt was still retrying. No RabbitMQ config, TLS/CA setup, or management-interface restriction was ever attempted.

evidence.finding: A foreground `apt-get update` blocked for 125s and was killed by the platform's 120-second proxy read timeout, before any install work began.
Executor had to pkill apt-get and clear dpkg/apt lock files (return_code 137/Killed) before retrying, indicating the first attempt left the package manager in a locked state.

evidence.source: repeated poll records across node1/node2/node3 from ~01:55 to 02:07 UTC
evidence.finding: Background `apt-get install` on all three nodes ran for 14+ minutes and repeatedly logged 'Unable to connect to archive.ubuntu.com:http', 'Connection failed', and 'connection timed out' against multiple mirror IPs (91.189.91.82, 91.189.92.23/24, 185.125.190.81/82/83), i.e., intermittent reachability to Ubuntu package mirrors from inside the cluster.

evidence.source: install log tail on node1, last selected record
evidence.finding: apt-get ultimately reported 'E: Failed to fetch ... rabbitmq-server_3.5.7-1ubuntu0.16.04.4_all.deb Unable to connect' and 'Unable to fetch some archives' — the install did not complete on node1 by the end of the selected evidence.

evidence.source: package list in the install log
evidence.finding: apt is resolving and attempting to fetch i386 (32-bit) packages (e.g., 'openssl i386', 'erlang-base i386') alongside the normal packages, which roughly doubles the number of archive fetches needed and thus doubles exposure to the flaky mirror connectivity.

Attempt ended via `executor_timed_out` / 'claude-code timed out after 2100 seconds' with no structured report returned, confirming the run was consumed entirely by the stuck package installation loop.

likely_causes.cause: Intermittent/flaky outbound network connectivity from the cluster nodes to the Ubuntu archive/security mirrors (repeated connection failures and timeouts to several different mirror IPs across all three nodes), independent of anything the executor did wrong in its commands.

An unnecessary i386 multiarch entry left enabled on the base image caused apt to also resolve/fetch i386 duplicates of every package, roughly doubling the number of downloads needed and thus doubling the chance of hitting the flaky mirror during the available time.

The executor's overall time budget (35 minutes) was consumed by polling a slow/failing apt process without switching strategy (e.g., retry with --fix-missing, alternate mirror, or apt.conf retry/timeout tuning), so even if the mirror stabilized shortly after, the task ran out of time before install, let alone TLS/CA/config work, could start.

EOL distro (Ubuntu 16.04 xenial) reaching end-of-life mirrors that may be more congested/less reliable than current-release mirrors, plausibly contributing to but not solely explaining the connection failures.

next_attempt_guidance: Before running any install, do a quick reachability check on all three nodes (e.g., `curl -sS -m 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://archive.ubuntu.com`) and only proceed once mirrors are confirmed reachable; if not, retry with backoff rather than launching a long apt-get immediately.

Never run `apt-get update`/`install` as a blocking foreground exec — use the background+redirect+poll pattern from the start (this run only adopted it after the first call hit the 120s proxy timeout).

Check for and drop unnecessary foreign architectures before installing: `dpkg --print-foreign-architectures` and, if i386 is listed and not needed, `dpkg --remove-architecture i386` (only if no i386 packages are already installed) to roughly halve the packages apt must fetch.

If mirror connectivity is flaky, add resilience to the apt invocation: `Acquire::Retries=5`, `Acquire::http::Timeout=30`, and run `apt-get install --fix-missing` in a small retry loop across nodes rather than a single multi-minute attempt.

Run the three-node installs in parallel (as this attempt did) but checkpoint progress more frequently and set an internal budget (e.g., abandon/retry after 5–8 minutes of no forward progress) instead of polling the same stalled process for 14+ minutes.

Only after rabbitmq-server + erlang are confirmed installed (`dpkg -l | grep rabbitmq-server` succeeds, `rabbitmqctl status` responds) proceed to: generate a private CA with openssl, issue per-node server certs and client certs signed by that CA, configure `listeners.ssl.default`, `ssl_options.cacertfile/certfile/keyfile`, `ssl_options.verify = verify_peer`, `ssl_options.fail_if_no_peer_cert = true` in rabbitmq.conf, form the cluster via Erlang cookie sync and `rabbitmqctl join_cluster`, and bind/firewall the management plugin (port 15672) to the cluster's internal network only.

There is no evidence in the audit about DNS resolution details, whether a proxy/NAT was involved, or whether the mirror failures were transient — if the same flakiness recurs on a fresh cluster, escalate as a possible platform/network issue rather than continuing to retry apt indefinitely.
